Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript, Nxeon hosting platform). FIRST STEP: create your own isolated git worktree:
  cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-modehero -b feature/freemc-mode-hero main
Then `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-modehero`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules`, `ln -s /opt/nxeon/.env .env`. Do all work there, not in /opt/nxeon directly.

CONTEXT: The free Minecraft product (`lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`'s `FREEMC_PRESETS`) has 8 plugin-based game modes that currently have NO visual identity beyond a text label: SkyBlock, Prison, Towny, Parkour, Anarchy, Lifesteal SMP, Missile Wars, Survival Games (plus 4 simple properties-only modes: Vanilla, Creative, Hardcore, Peaceful, which are lower priority but could use something too if time allows). The user wants hero images for these — currently `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx`'s `Overview` component and `components/customer/FreeMinecraftPanel.tsx`'s create-form both render these as plain text cards with no imagery.

READ FIRST for existing visual conventions: `public/games/art/` — every PAID game already has `<slug>_hero.jpg` (1920x1080 or similar wide hero), `<slug>_poster.jpg` (portrait cover), and `public/logos/games/` has small logo PNGs. Look at a couple of existing hero images (e.g. `minecraft_hero.jpg`, `rust_hero.jpg`) to understand the established crop/style. Also read `app/(marketing)/free-minecraft/page.tsx` and `components/marketing/GameHero.tsx` to see how hero art is actually consumed/rendered on the marketing side, for context on sizing/aspect ratio expectations.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT — read before sourcing anything: these are GAME MODES (gameplay concepts within Minecraft), not separate licensed games, so there is no official promotional art for "Nxeon SkyBlock" etc. to find. Do NOT scrape or reuse actual Minecraft screenshots/gameplay footage from the web for these — that's Mojang-copyrighted material and not something to source via generic image search for a commercial product. Two acceptable paths, pick per-mode based on what you can actually produce well:
1. **Preferred: generate clean, on-brand illustrated/stylized hero art** — abstract or geometric compositions that evoke each mode's theme (a floating island silhouette for SkyBlock, prison bars/mine-cart imagery for Prison, a small town/banner motif for Towny, a checkered/gap-jump pattern for Parkour, a cracked/danger motif for Anarchy, a heart/life motif for Lifesteal SMP, a missile/arena motif for Missile Wars, an arena/last-one-standing motif for Survival Games) rendered as SVG or Canvas art matching the Nxeon brand palette (navy background, violet/cyan accents — see [[marketing design]] convention: gradients like `from-accent-blue/90 to-brand-500/90`, deep navy `~#0a0e1a`, violet `~#6f47f5`, cyan/blue `~#3b82f6`). This keeps everything license-clean and visually consistent as a set (a "family" of 8 hero images that clearly belong together).
2. If you find genuinely royalty-free/CC0 stock photography that thematically fits (NOT Minecraft-specific, e.g. a generic "floating island" or "medieval town" landscape photo) and looks premium enough, that's acceptable too — but verify the license explicitly and note the source.

Do NOT half-ship a placeholder gradient with just text — either produce real illustrated/generated imagery or genuinely licensed stock, not a lorem-ipsum-tier stand-in.

DELIVERABLE:
1. Produce 8 hero images (1920x1080 or matching the existing convention you find), one per plugin-based mode, saved to `public/games/art/freemc-<mode>_hero.jpg` (or `.png` if the format needs transparency) — pick filenames that clearly indicate they're mode-specific, not full-game art (e.g. `freemc-skyblock_hero.jpg`).
2. Wire them in: add a `heroImage?: string` field to the `FreeMcPreset` type in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` and set it on each of the 8 plugin presets (leave the 4 properties-only ones without one, or add simple ones too if you have time — your call, note which you did).
3. Update the Overview preset-card grid in `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` and the create-form picker in `components/customer/FreeMinecraftPanel.tsx` to actually render the hero image (e.g. as a card background or a small thumbnail — match the existing card layout, don't redesign the whole card structure, just add the image).
4. `npx tsc --noEmit` and a full `npm run build` must both pass clean.
5. Commit your work explicitly (`git add` named files, never `-A`) so it's not lost. Do not merge to main, do not delete your worktree — I'll integrate it.

Report back: how you produced each image (generated/illustrated vs. sourced stock, and license if stock), the file paths, and confirmation build/typecheck passed.
